Seminar Title:

Characterization of the Laser-Powder Bed Fused Ti-6Al-4V Part

Seminar Type:

Abstract:

The ASTM Grade 5 titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V also known as Ti64) is an alpha-beta titanium alloy which possesses a high specific strength (strength-to-weight ratio) and outstanding resistance against corrosion. Due to its low density and excellent corrosion resistance, this alloy finds widespread engineering applications especially in the aerospace industries and biomedical sectors (for manufacturing implants and prostheses). The alloys low modulus of elasticity, poor thermal conductivity, and strong chemical reactivity (towards the cutting tool/ tool coating materials) invite several challenges during the traditional subtractive (machining) of Ti64 parts. Nevertheless, traditional manufacturing techniques often fail to fabricate intricate designed (high definition) custom parts with graded porosity and tailored material properties. In this context, the Additive Manufacturing (AM) has the potential to replace the traditional methods of fabrication. In contrast to the subtractive manufacturing, AM builds parts through a layer-upon-layer deposition fashion. Since the process-mechanism and thermal history of the AM techniques are entirely different than the traditional casting, forging, and machining processes, it is utmost important to go for characterization of the additively built part before the parts are subjected to real life applications. In the present work, the Laser-Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) process is attempted to fabricate Ti64 parts. The task of fabrication is carried out at varied scanning speeds whilst laser power, hatch distance, scan pattern, and layer thickness are kept constant. Microstructural, micro-hardness, and tribological characteristics of the L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V alloy are characterized at the as built state, especially focusing on the impact of scan speed (900 and 1200 mm/s). Effect of post-heat treatment on the material characteristics is also studied. Tribological performance is examined through scratch tests.
